name: Wei Gao
title: Professor
department: Electrical and Computer Engineering; Intelligent Systems Laboratory
fitReason: Strong software-first match for a CS master’s researcher: multi-view geometric reasoning, efficient VLM deployment and language-grounded assistive interaction. A compact perception/model-evaluation project fits better than building new clinical hardware or launching a patient trial.

physicalEvidence.summary: The April 2026 Pitt paper coauthored with Dan Ding describes Stretch 3 in a mock kitchen. Manipulation is Wizard-of-Oz teleoperated; navigation and communication are autonomous. Participants evaluated prerecorded robot videos and generated policies, not live robot interactions. This collaborative setup supports a physical-robot connection without proving Gao’s own robot inventory or visitor access.

shortVisit.summary: His current university-hosted homepage invites interested students to send a CV and transcript, but does not specify external visitors, internships, duration or summer 2027 availability. Pitt’s general international visitor rules may provide an administrative route after host acceptance; they do not establish this lab’s availability. The separate RST research intake is not a confirmed Gao/ECE placement route.

scoreReasons.fit: strong 3D/VLM, efficient AI and language-personalization overlap.
scoreReasons.physical: collaborative real-robot video-based research with teleoperated manipulation; own-lab access unknown.

unknowns: Do not confuse this Pitt ECE professor with same-name researchers elsewhere; current institutional profile, personal homepage and paper affiliation agree.
The study’s simulated meal-preparation language denotes a mock task environment; it uses robot video stimuli and Wizard-of-Oz manipulation, not demonstrated autonomous LLM-to-motor execution.
Current project-page research in spatial reasoning is largely model/system evaluation; it is not automatically physical robot experimentation.
International appointment, eight-week supervision, funding, self-funded status and permitted nonclinical activity require host and OIS approval.
Public robot research does not confirm current equipment access, a summer 2027 offer or host availability.
